subject: Streaming chat latency: investigation, mitigations, and postmortem
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@cloudcart.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden increase in streaming latency for chat endpoints

Hi Rafael,

We started seeing large spikes in tail latency for our live chat sessions around 17:55 UTC. The stream either pauses for 5–15s or delivers chunks in very small bursts — this is causing visible UI stalls for customers. It started at roughly 17:55 and affected ~30% of sessions for about 35 minutes.

We've collected client-side timings and sent a support dump (ops@cloudcart.com) but wanted to flag this here since it impacted a number of paying customers today. Can you confirm whether Redwood saw anything region-wide or if this looks like an edge/regional issue?

App: CloudCart support chat (prod)
Region: us-east-1
Requests affected: streaming.chat.generate with model=rwd-8b-lowlatency
Impact: UI stalls, several customer escalations in support queue

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
Senior SRE, CloudCart

Attachment: client_timings_20260816.log (referenced in ops ticket)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 18:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden increase in streaming latency for chat endpoints

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the log dump. We're investigating now and want to give you immediate mitigations while we dig in.

Summary of immediate actions you can take (low-risk, reversible):
- Switch to non-streaming responses temporarily (chat.generate -> chat.complete mode) to avoid chunking stalls.
- Reduce max_tokens to 256 for live sessions to lower KV cache pressure and token bursts.
- Pin to model variant rwd-8b-lowlatency-v2 (we've seen v2 favor smaller per-token compute) — change only for live-critical routes.
- Enable request-level prefix caching ("prefix_cache": "session") in your SDK config to reduce cold-start token work.
- If you use a single long-lived socket, add an application-side 3s chunk timeout and retry a new request on timeout; this masks intermittent pauses.

I'll summarize the more technical findings as soon as Ben has the root cause. In the meantime I've attached an excerpt of relevant server logs we've requested from our edge fleet and a small config patch you can test.

Attachments: support_log_excerpt.txt (server-side timestamps), config_patch.diff (example toggles)

Short ETA: we expect a targeted mitigation rollout in us-east-1 within 60–90 minutes if the root cause is confirmed. I'll loop back with precise RCA and recommended permanent fixes.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0193
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 19:10:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: quick tech note on us-east-1 streaming degradation

Rafael / Monica / Laura — quick internal summary from the infra side (putting notes here so Rafael can translate outward):
- Timeline: 17:48 UTC autoscaling event in us-east-1 triggered rebalancing of several shard groups. During the rebalance we observed a KV-cache eviction storm on nodes serving rwd-8b-lowlatency (cache thrash + increased GC pauses).
- Effect: increased per-request setup time and more frequent small chunk flushes; streams didn't drop entirely but throughput was choppy (client-observed 5–15s stalls).
- Root cause: a combination of a recent kernel-level thread scheduler change (rolled earlier in the day) and a mis-sized cache watermark for this model's shard layout. The scheduler change increased latency variance under simultaneous GC pressure.
- Short-term mitigation we pushed (18:05 UTC): raised cache high-watermark for affected shard pool, limited concurrent batch size to 32, and pinned a subset of traffic to nodes running the older scheduler config. These measures reduced observed client stalls by ~80% within 20 minutes.
- Next steps (planned):
  - Revert the scheduler roll for the remainder of the fleet pending a corrected rollout (INF-3721).
  - Adjust cache watermark heuristics for rwd-8b family (follow-up patch scheduled for 2026-08-18).
  - Add a streaming health metric that surfaces chunk inter-arrival variance to the status page.

I'll prepare a short postmortem note and a minimal runbook for customers outlining recommended client-side fallbacks.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@cloudcart.com>, ops@cloudcart.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Postmortem and customer runbook — 2026-08-16 us-east-1 streaming latency

Alex / CloudCart ops team —

Thanks again for flagging this. Below is a short postmortem and an operational runbook you can use if you see similar symptoms in the future. We sincerely regret the customer impact; our team committed a partial incident credit for the affected window and we've shared a PDF postmortem (attached).

What happened (TL;DR) - Around 17:48 UTC on 2026-08-16 an autoscale and scheduler rollout coincided causing excessive KV-cache evictions for nodes serving the rwd-8b-lowlatency model in us-east-1. The eviction storm led to chunking and small-burst delivery behavior for streaming responses, producing visible UI stalls for some sessions.

Actions we took - Immediate: raised shard cache watermarks, limited concurrent batch sizes for the affected pool, and pinned a subset of traffic to nodes running the pre-roll scheduler. These reduced customer-stated stalls by ~80% within 20 minutes.
- Short-term: rolled back the scheduler change fleet-wide at 08:22 UTC and applied a conservative cache watermark.
- Long-term: a follow-up rolling change to the cache heuristics, a scheduler-change canary gating improvement, and a new streaming health metric (INF-3721).

Customer runbook (recommended short-term mitigations for streaming latency)
1) Switch to non-streaming mode for degraded user flows: chat.complete (clients should fall back to single-response mode)
2) Reduce max_tokens to 256 or lower for live/interactive sessions during incidents
3) Use model pinning to rwd-8b-lowlatency-v2 or a smaller model family when latency is critical
4) Enable session-level prefix_cache in the SDK to reduce repeated context work
5) Implement a client-side chunk-timeout of ~3s and retry as a new request to recover from pauses
6) If you have multi-region routing, failover to another region (us-west-2) for live-critical traffic if latency is unacceptable

Compensation & next steps - We've opened INF-3721 in our internal tracker and will share the full RCA when complete. The attached postmortem contains timelines and telemetry excerpts. Redwood will apply a usage credit for the 17:48–18:23 UTC window for sessions that reported chunking behavior; your ops contact will receive the credit estimate shortly.

If you'd like, Monica and I can set up a 30-min run-through with your SREs to walk the runbook and test the config patch on a staging environment.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachments: postmortem-20260817.pdf
